resources.string: Log in to an existing account
There is no vault on this device yet. Creating one keeps the entries here, and the codes are computed offline.

Note: this machine has no platform key store, so the master key will be written to a file that only your operating system account can read. Continuing means you accept that; TPM support is not wired in yet.

Logging in takes the master key from a device that is already unlocked: that device shows a code, this one turns it into a request, and the reply comes back after the other side confirms. The master key travels out of band, through the code, and never through a server.
The vault is locked. Unlocking takes the master key out of the platform key store again; there is no password to type.

This device holds a master key that cannot be read right now. Creating a new vault here would replace it and its entries would be lost, so do not do that before trying the recovery key on another device.

This device holds a master key, but its vault file is gone. Logging in from another device of the same account brings the entries back; creating a vault here would draw a new key and cut this device off from the account.
Creation failed: the core cannot serialize the vault.
Creation failed: the platform key store is unavailable, and the core refused a local-only vault as well.
Locked automatically after being open for %1$d seconds
No entries yet. Use + to scan a QR code or to enter a secret by hand.
The link is filled in already when the clipboard holds one.
This is not an otpauth:// link, or its parameters are not accepted (the secret must be valid Base32).
Every device this account syncs with deletes them too, and a code cannot be recovered once the entry is gone.
Copied; the clipboard is cleared again after 30 seconds.
No image was read (the dialog was cancelled, or the file cannot be decoded).
This image holds no readable entry code (an otpauth:// QR code is expected).
The entry was not accepted: the secret or the parameters are not valid.
Nothing was saved: the secret or the parameters are not accepted (the secret must be valid Base32).
Choose an image holding a QR code
Syncing moves codes in both directions: one device shows a code, the other reads it and merges what it carries. Nothing goes through a server, and the codes are the only thing that travels.
This device has no platform identity, so it cannot sync. It was created as a local-only vault, which cannot pair or sync.
Hand this code to the other device. After a merge, generate it again: what you hand over is the state at the moment it was generated.
Read the other device's code: paste it below, or open the image it was saved as.
The sync code was read from the image.
This image holds no readable sync code.
This code was not accepted: it is not a sync code, or it does not belong to this account.
This code claims a sender the channel does not confirm, so it was refused.
There was nothing to read: paste or scan the other device's code first.
This code did not authenticate: it was not written with this account's master key.
The code could not be merged.
The merge could not be saved on this device.
Nothing new: this device already had everything that code carried.
The two devices disagree about %1$d of them; decide below.
The other device deleted this entry; this one still has it.
This device deleted this entry; the other one still has it.
This device's version is the later one.
The decision could not be applied, so nothing was changed.
The other device shows a request after reading the pairing code; the master key leaves this device only when you confirm.
Pairing cannot start: this machine has no usable platform key store.
Hand the pairing code below to the new device (it is valid for this step only). Once it has read the code, it gives you a request.
The request from the new device
This image holds no readable request.
The request was read from the image.
This request is not accepted: it may not belong to this pairing.
Authorize this device (hand the master key to this session)
Requester identity: %1$s. Hand the reply below to it to finish; nothing has been given to it before that.
Authorized. Hand the reply below to the new device to finish.
On a device that is already unlocked, choose “Pair a new device”, then paste the pairing code it shows below.
This image holds no readable pairing code.
The pairing code was read from the image.
This is not a usable pairing code, or this machine has no usable platform key store.
The request cannot be generated: the platform key store refused the operation.
Hand the text below back to that device:
This image holds no readable reply.
The reply was read from the image.
The reply did not verify: it may not belong to this pairing, or the passphrase or the session does not match.
Login succeeded, but the vault cannot be serialized.
In the platform key store, hardware protected
In a file on this device, protected by your operating system account only
None: this vault cannot pair or sync
A recovery key file together with a passphrase you choose can restore the master key if every device is lost. Keep it offline: whoever holds the file and the passphrase holds the account.
The two passphrases are not the same.
The recovery key could not be created.
The recovery key could not be saved.
The file could not be read.
Not accepted: the passphrase is wrong, or this file is not a recovery key.
Importing an account's recovery key replaces what is on this device with that account. Entries that exist only here are not merged, and are lost.
The application is Apache-2.0; the Rust layers it builds on are LGPL-3.0-or-later.

Deletes this device's vault and master key, so that it can register again or log in from another device. Entries that were not exported or synced are lost. The device identity in the platform key store is kept: this repairs the account, not the identity.
The vault file and the master key on this device are deleted. If no other device holds this account and no recovery key file exists, its entries are gone for good.
The master key and the vault were removed. This device is back to its first run.
Hold the code in the frame, or read one out of an image.
Read the code out of an image
The camera was not allowed, so the code has to come from an image.
The camera would not start, so the code has to come from an image.
The deletion reaches every device this account is on: the entry disappears there as well, and the codes it produced cannot be recovered.
